samples.extra: Congenital: … (then subaortic stenosis, pulmonic stenosis). Acquired: … (~75% of canine heart disease); DCM second, in large breeds.

samples.text: Puppy, continuous "machinery" murmur loudest at left heart base, bounding water-hammer pulses → {{c1::PDA}} {{c2::left atrium and left ventricle}}
samples.extra: Left-to-right …; aorta-to-PA shunt volume-overloads the … (pulmonary overcirculation). Close early by surgical ligation or transcatheter occluder (ACDO); ~65% untreated die within 1 year. Females, Poodles, Maltese, Pomeranians, Shelties; heritable — do not breed.

samples.text: DV radiograph: bulges at aortic arch (1 o'clock), pulmonary trunk (2 o'clock), left auricle (3 o'clock) plus a "ductus bump" on the descending aorta → {{c1::PDA radiographic triad with pulmonary overcirculation; ECG tall R waves (>3 mV), wide P mitrale. Confirm by echo: continuous turbulent flow in the pulmonary artery.}}
Dog with known PDA whose murmur disappeared; hindlimb weakness, cyanotic caudal membranes with pink oral membranes, polycythemia → {{c1::differential cyanosis}} {{c2::Do not ligate}}
samples.extra: Reversed (right-to-left) PDA from pulmonary hypertension — …. … (fatal right heart failure); phlebotomy or hydroxyurea for PCV >65%, sildenafil.

samples.text: Soft grade I–II systolic murmur in a puppy that fades by 4–6 months → {{c1::Innocent (physiologic) murmur; no workup if it disappears. Loud, continuous or persistent murmurs need echocardiography.}}

Young Boxer/Golden/Newfoundland/Rottweiler, systolic ejection murmur at left base (ICS 3–4) radiating to carotids, weak late-rising pulses → Subaortic stenosis {{c1::— the congenital defect most often causing exertional syncope and sudden death (ischemic ventricular arrhythmias); predisposes to endocarditis. Doppler >4.5 m/s = severe; atenolol.}}
Young Bulldog/Boxer/Beagle, systolic murmur at left base (ICS 2–3), right axis deviation/RV hypertrophy, normal femoral pulses → Pulmonic stenosis {{c1::>50–80 mmHg}}
samples.extra: ; balloon valvuloplasty when gradient … (caution: anomalous coronary artery in Bulldogs). Not weak femoral pulses — those point to subaortic stenosis.
